output.summary: The rise in admitted-patient ED length of stay is almost entirely boarding (E5). ED RN hours per visit, vacancy and grid compliance are flat or better (E4), and volume, acuity and bed capacity are unchanged (E3, E9). That contradicts the understaffing, volume and capacity hypotheses. Boarding jumped in March when the hospitalist rounding change took effect, and medical wards account for 81% of boarding hours. Discharges on those wards moved later while surgical wards did not (E8). The 4 West pilot ran on days set by an earlier rotation. Huddle days showed earlier discharges and shorter boarding, with no change on neighbouring wards (E10, E11). Extend the huddle. Do not fund travel nurses by deferring case managers, and do not pause the huddle. The evening cleaning cut is unmeasured.
